subject: Will different mapping methods give very different results?

messages.author: 2581d6401e41d682
messages.subject: Will different mapping methods give very different results?
parts:
Hi everyone,

Using the same dataset, I tried several different mapping methods,
e.g. hk in rqtl, interval mapping or CIM in QTL Cartography, and
regression or interval mapping in MapManager. But some of them gave
very different results. For example, on the same chromosome, I mapped
single peaks at different location or mapped multiple peaks. So I am
wondering what could be the reasons, and which method is best and
reliable. Thanks.

Jo

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Will different mapping methods give very different results?
parts:
Dear Jo,

It depends on a lot of things, particularly on marker density and the
pattern of missing genotypes. What sort of cross are you
considering? How many individuals? What marker density? Was a
selective genotyping strategy used? How much of the genotype data are
missing? What is the nature of the phenotype?

I would first separate the method (e.g. interval mapping or Haley-
Knott regression) from the implementation of that method (i.e., the
particular program).

In comparing results from R/qtl and Cartographer and MapManager, it
would be best to focus on using scanone with method="em", in R/qtl,
versus interval mapping in Cartographer or MapManager. In particular,
R/qtl and Cartographer should give you equivalent results.

Comparing Haley-Knott regression and standard interval mapping would
be best done within R/qtl (scanone with method="hk" vs method="em").

Comparing interval mapping and CIM would best be done within
Cartographer.

karl
